source.author: Vedic seers (traditional)
source.translator: F. Max Müller, 1879 & Swāmi Nikhilānanda (public domain portions)

entries.text: You are what your deep, driving desire is. As your desire is, so is your will. As your will is, so is your deed. As your deed is, so is your destiny.

entries.long: "Tat tvam asi." You are That — the deepest reality beneath everything is already who you are.

entries.text: From the unreal lead me to the real. From darkness lead me to light. From death lead me to immortality.
The Self is not to be known through study, nor through sharp intellect, nor through much hearing of sacred texts.
When all the desires that dwell in the heart fall away, then the mortal becomes immortal.
Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
As a man acts, so does he become. A man of good deeds becomes good, a man of bad deeds, bad.
He who knows the Self puts away all sorrow.
The Self is hidden in the hearts of all, as butter lies hidden in cream.
Let your aim be one and single. Let your heart be one, unified, whole.
As the rivers flowing east and west merge in the sea and become one with it, so do all beings merge into the Self.
Where there is duality, one sees another, hears another, knows another. Where everything is the Self, what could one see, hear, or know?
The knower of the Self overcomes grief.
The body is the bow, OM the arrow, and the Self the target. Hit the mark with intent undistracted.
Like two birds on the same tree: one eats the sweet fruit, the other watches without eating. So the Self and the soul sit side by side.
